# Nexus Code v1.1.1

**Maturity:** Stable release for Nexus Code v1.1.1.

This release delivers the complete Nexus Code multi-agent orchestration architecture, serialized git integration with verified execution receipts, typed inter-agent communication, operation replay, and closed edge cases for cancellation idempotency, message du
- Multi-agent orchestration with deterministic parallel work units and per-resource slot reservations.
- Serialized Git integration queue with candidate digests and verified execution receipts.
- Typed inter-agent communication channels (`request`, `observation`, `artifact`, `verdict`).
- Operation timeline replay with schema version 2 persistence and safe legacy migration.
- Cancellation idempotency and late result suppression.
- Durability-positive message acknowledgment and structured retry classification.
- Proven prompt submission provenance (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`) protecting message injection against model outputs, tool outputs, and non-Nexus user notes.
- Protected task envelope replay failure propagation across single- and multi-record queries.

## Runtime requirements

Unchanged from v1.0.0: Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (local or an explicitly selected provider). The archive does not include Node.js; Rust and Cargo are not required at runtime.

## Highlights

### Deterministic parallel work units

An operation may now run more than one work unit at a time:

```json
{
  "objective": "Add a --dry-run flag",
  "policy": { "maxConcurrentUnits": 2 },
  "resources": [
    { "id": "primary", "endpoint": "https://api.example/v1", "model": "m1" },
    { "id": "secondary", "endpoint": "https://api.example/v1", "model": "m2", "maxConcurrentUnits": 1 }
  ],
  "units": [
    { "id": "impl", "role": "implementer", "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "docs", "role": "implementer", "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "test", "role": "tester", "dependsOn": ["impl"], "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "review", "role": "reviewer", "dependsOn": ["impl", "test"], "requires": { "independentOf": ["impl"] } }
  ]
}
```

- The scheduler returns an ordered due-set: required units first, then the longest unfinished dependent chain, then the operation's declared unit order. The same persisted state always produces the same due-set.
- Concurrency defaults to **1**. An operation that does not opt in behaves as it did in v1.0.0: one unit in flight.
- Per-resource slots are reserved for the duration of a run, so two units pinned to one single-slot resource serialise. A unit whose qualified slots are busy stays `RUNNABLE` — it is not parked and not escalated.
- One unit's failure does not touch a batch-mate. Cancelling aborts every in-flight unit and leaves each resumable. A restart reconciles every unit that was in flight.

### Retained worktrees are named

A unit worktree with uncommitted or ignored files is kept rather than destroyed, and the event log now says which worktree was kept and why (`WORKTREE_RETAINED`). A clean lifecycle still leaves no unit worktree behind.

### Serialised git integration with evidenced receipts

Concurrent isolated units complete at unpredictable times, but they share one integration worktree. Integration is now a queue: one merge at a time, in completion order, with `INTEGRATION_QUEUED` and `INTEGRATION_SKIPPED` events. Each receipt records:

- the unit's branch and commit, and the resulting `integratedCommit`;
- the **candidate digest** of the tree that was merged (omitted, never fabricated, when the worktree was already gone);
- the **executed verifier** the unit was accepted with (omitted when it produced none);
- a 1-based **sequence** so a reviewer can reconstruct merge order.

### Typed messages between units
# Nexus Code v1.1.2 Roadmap: Specialist Orchestration & Independent Review

**Milestone:** Nexus Code `v1.1.2`  
**Status:** In Progress  
**Owner:** Principal Software Architect & Senior Implementation Engineer  
**Document ID:** `NEXUS-ROADMAP-V112`  
**Base Release:** `v1.1.1` (`b9dd0bcc`) / `v1.1.2-rc.1` (`c3e26103`)  

---

## 1. Roadmap Overview & Commitments

The v1.1.2 release line encompasses two complementary tiers:
1. **Tier 1 (Completed in v1.1.2-rc.1):** Operational defect fix for multi-message prompt deduplication upon crash-resume ([PR #377](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/pull/377)) and release documentation addendum.
2. **Tier 2 (v1.1.2 Feature Enhancement):** Bounded specialist agent contracts, objective independent review boundaries (eliminating implementer confirmation bias), deterministic micro-routing (cut from PR #396), and telemetry-aware scheduling.

### Status in PR #396 (owner decision: connect the new modules or cut them)
- **Item 1, connected.** The specialist contracts are runtime roles in `cli/src/core/roles.ts`. An operation unit or `/team` target can run as one. The agent offers only the contract's permitted tools, and it refuses any other call when the call is dispatched (`roleToolAllowList`). That holds whethe
- **Item 2, connected.** Units with the `reviewer` or `acceptance_reviewer` role run behind the boundary:
  - Their prompt is the evidence package: the candidate diff against the operation's base commit, and the verifier receipt of the unit they depend on. Prerequisite summaries are withheld.
  - The unit completes only on a well-formed `ACCEPT` that survives the deterministic gates. Prose, a malformed verdict, a reported defect or a failed verifier blocks the unit for an operator decision.
  - The verifier receipt comes from the dependency's integration receipt (isolated operations) or, where nothing was integrated (for example `/team`), from the verification recorded on the dependency's completed result. A verification that is not a passing run that executed tests reaches the package
  - Retrying a rejected review resumes the reviewer's conversation. A review unit or read-only specialist (`reviewer`, `acceptance_reviewer`, `semantic_explorer`, `call_site_analyzer`, `security_reviewer`; read-only by construction) does not inherit the write-verification obligation that recovery ad
  - The base a review diffs against is the isolated operation's base commit or, for a non-isolated operation in a Git checkout, the HEAD recorded when the operation first ran (`startCommit`), so a change a unit committed is still in the diff. The base is recorded only before any unit has started; an
  - `security_reviewer` is deliberately not behind the boundary: only `reviewer` and `acceptance_reviewer` are. It is a read-only specialist whose contract lists `unified_diff` as an input, and it keeps the ordinary prompt.
  - An empty candidate diff is treated as a failure to collect evidence (there is nothing to judge), and the worst verification across all dependencies decides the verifier exit code.
  - If the candidate diff cannot be collected (no Git checkout, or the diff exceeds the 4 MiB buffer), the review is blocked before any model turn. That failure is never presented to the reviewer as evidence.
  - The runtime package names the real operation id and declares no file scope: no operation or unit declares one, so the scope gate (`detectScopeViolations`) applies only to a package that supplies `authorizedScope`.
  - The boundary complements `cli/src/core/independent_check.ts`, which decides whether a verifier pass is independent evidence. It does not replace it.
- **Items 3 and 4, cut.** Nothing in the runtime routed on the micro-router. The escalation machine duplicated the non-progress recovery in PR #398, which is connected.
- **`TokenBudgetTracker`, cut.** It duplicated `UsageLedger` (`cli/src/usage.ts`), which already enforces `NEXUS_CLOUD_MAX_TOKENS` with in-flight reservations.
- **Integrated with PR #398.** The recovery context's "Permitted next actions" lists only actions the agent's role and mode allow (`renderRecoveryContext`'s `permits` predicate).
- **Item 5 and the CERI and comparative harness entry points are not yet connected.** The throttle needs request latency from `cli/src/client.ts`. CERI needs a `nexus eval` command in `cli/src/index.ts`. Both files are claimed by other open work.

---

## 2. Workstream Roadmap Specifications

# Nexus Code v1.1.1

**Maturity:** Stable release for Nexus Code v1.1.1.

This release delivers the complete Nexus Code multi-agent orchestration architecture, serialized git integration with verified execution receipts, typed inter-agent communication, operation replay, and closed edge cases for cancellation idempotency, message du
- Multi-agent orchestration with deterministic parallel work units and per-resource slot reservations.
- Serialized Git integration queue with candidate digests and verified execution receipts.
- Typed inter-agent communication channels (`request`, `observation`, `artifact`, `verdict`).
- Operation timeline replay with schema version 2 persistence and safe legacy migration.
- Cancellation idempotency and late result suppression.
- Durability-positive message acknowledgment and structured retry classification.
- Proven prompt submission provenance (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`) protecting message injection against model outputs, tool outputs, and non-Nexus user notes.
- Protected task envelope replay failure propagation across single- and multi-record queries.

## Runtime requirements

Unchanged from v1.0.0: Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (local or an explicitly selected provider). The archive does not include Node.js; Rust and Cargo are not required at runtime.

## Highlights

### Deterministic parallel work units

An operation may now run more than one work unit at a time:

```json
{
  "objective": "Add a --dry-run flag",
  "policy": { "maxConcurrentUnits": 2 },
  "resources": [
    { "id": "primary", "endpoint": "https://api.example/v1", "model": "m1" },
    { "id": "secondary", "endpoint": "https://api.example/v1", "model": "m2", "maxConcurrentUnits": 1 }
  ],
  "units": [
    { "id": "impl", "role": "implementer", "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "docs", "role": "implementer", "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "test", "role": "tester", "dependsOn": ["impl"], "prompt": "…" },
    { "id": "review", "role": "reviewer", "dependsOn": ["impl", "test"], "requires": { "independentOf": ["impl"] } }
  ]
}
```

- The scheduler returns an ordered due-set: required units first, then the longest unfinished dependent chain, then the operation's declared unit order. The same persisted state always produces the same due-set.
- Concurrency defaults to **1**. An operation that does not opt in behaves as it did in v1.0.0: one unit in flight.
- Per-resource slots are reserved for the duration of a run, so two units pinned to one single-slot resource serialise. A unit whose qualified slots are busy stays `RUNNABLE` — it is not parked and not escalated.
- One unit's failure does not touch a batch-mate. Cancelling aborts every in-flight unit and leaves each resumable. A restart reconciles every unit that was in flight.

### Retained worktrees are named

A unit worktree with uncommitted or ignored files is kept rather than destroyed, and the event log now says which worktree was kept and why (`WORKTREE_RETAINED`). A clean lifecycle still leaves no unit worktree behind.

### Serialised git integration with evidenced receipts

Concurrent isolated units complete at unpredictable times, but they share one integration worktree. Integration is now a queue: one merge at a time, in completion order, with `INTEGRATION_QUEUED` and `INTEGRATION_SKIPPED` events. Each receipt records:

- the unit's branch and commit, and the resulting `integratedCommit`;
- the **candidate digest** of the tree that was merged (omitted, never fabricated, when the worktree was already gone);
- the **executed verifier** the unit was accepted with (omitted when it produced none);
- a 1-based **sequence** so a reviewer can reconstruct merge order.

The WP-1107 gate is not clean, so the release is still waiting. Nothing is tagged, and `v1/v112-wp1101-integration` still has nothing committed or pushed past `3eea888a`.

At 23:00 UTC codex-root released SUITE after a failed gate. `make test` exited 2 with 2345 tests: 2307 pass, 33 fail and 5 skipped, and the terminal-scope and security stages weren't reached. I read the log (`/tmp/wp1107-full-gate-final4.log`) read-only. The failures fall into two groups:

- **Tests of real provider behaviour:** server context discovery, standalone profiles, and tokenize on llama.cpp and vLLM. Others cover Ollama recognition, vLLM `max_model_len` in `/v1/models`, and the `/model` provider-switch flow. They sit alongside the shared test fixtures, so the WP-1107 provider-identity change is changing how existing providers are recognised.
- **Eval suites:** `eval_integrity`, `eval_harness`, `eval_hardened`, `eval_t3`, `eval_dataset` and `eval_version_probe_storage`. This looks like the same cause, since the eval model proxy fixtures are affected too.

At 23:05 UTC, codex-root claimed the test files and the eval proxy for "WP-1107 handshake fixture corrections" and "provider identity fixture endpoints". Updating fixtures to match a deliberate new rule is legitimate. Updating them so a regression passes would not be, and your standing rule is no weakened assertions. I can't tell which this is from the log. The independent reviewer I spawn at the exact head will have to check that, and it is the main review risk for this release.

- **Cost:** this is exactly the work that took a full qualification cycle to get right for RC2, and these new failures reopen it. If the fixture fixes don't settle it soon, deferring WP-1107 to 1.1.3 is still the quicker route to a tag. That's your call, and I'll keep following your current decision unless you change it.
- **Still holding:** the version and qualification files remain claimed by codex-root. The SUITE claim is currently free.
- **#402:** unchanged, with all checks passing except Entire Gates, which is pending.

I'll check again at 23:41 UTC.

content.text:
I read that as codex-root's own status. It is the right call and it delays the release, but nothing for me to do yet.

- **The flaw:** the provider-matrix runner could accept a runtime supplied by the caller after it had verified the installed candidate. Its results could then describe different code from the one that was verified. This is the evidence for the G1.1-4 constrained-decoding gate, so the flaw matters.
- **What codex-root is doing:** writing a regression test first, then the smallest fix, then rerunning the gates. That is the order I'd want.
- **What it changes:** the `final5` and `final6` full-suite results do not cover the matrix runner as it will be fixed. The final gate has to be run on the fixed commit, so the commit I'm waiting for is further off than the 1-failure `final5` result suggested.
- **For the independent reviewer:** the exact-head review will have to check this boundary specifically. It must confirm the matrix runner only ever runs the installed candidate and cannot be pointed at other code, and that the regression test fails without the fix.

The claims are unchanged, so I still can't start the bump or the suite. I haven't touched anything. My scheduled check is at 01:14 UTC, and I'll look for the fixed commit and the released claims then.

<result>## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES for 5fde750a

The focused tests pass, but I found one functional regression on the vLLM path and two real gaps in the other areas you asked about. I worked in detached worktrees (`~/nexus-wt/rv-wp1107` at 5fde750a, plus a temporary baseline at 3eea888a) with a throwaway HOME. I removed both worktrees at the end. I touched nothing under `eval/`; I copied the matrix files to the scratchpad for mutation tests. I did not print any token or secret.

## Findings, by severity

**HIGH: vLLM strict mode makes `write_file` and `run_command` fail at execution.**
- `cli/src/core/tool_grammar_provider.ts:35-41` turns every optional parameter into a required, nullable one. A strict-mode model will therefore emit `"overwrite": null`, `"background": null` and similar.
- The Rust core rejects those nulls. `core/src/file_ops.rs` declares `overwrite: bool`, and `core/src/runner.rs` declares `timeout_secs: u64`, `shell: String` and `background: bool`.
- I built the core from this commit and called `RustCoreBridge.executeTool` directly:
  - `write_file {overwrite:null}` returns `Invalid write_file arguments: invalid type: null, expected a boolean`.
  - `run_command` with `background:null` returns `Invalid run_command arguments: invalid type: null, expected a boolean`, and all-null fails the same way.
  - `timeout_secs`, `shell`, `cwd` and `service_name` as null each succeed on their own, as do `read_file` and `edit_file` nulls.
- Nothing in `client.ts` (around 1526 and 1792), `agent.ts` (`dispatchToolCallImpl`, around 4850) or the `executeTool` pipeline strips nulls before dispatch. I traced the agent path by reading it, not by running a full agent loop against a mock vLLM.
- The matrix would not catch this. It classifies a call as `native_valid` when it satisfies the adapted schema, and that schema allows null (`validateToolArguments` and its test at `tool_grammar_matrix.test.mjs:130`). A vLLM lane could score 100% while every `write_file` and `run_command` call fails when executed.
- The fix is to strip nulls for fields that were optional before the adapter ran. Do it in the client or the dispatch path, or make the core accept null.

**MEDIUM: REQ-PRV-109 holds only on the success path.**
- `routingHeaders()` (`client.ts:809-821`) suppresses X-Task-Class only when the cached kind is known. The commit now demotes the kind to `unknown` whenever a handshake fails, so the header is sent to a standalone server.
- I ran the same scenarios at base and head with a `taskClass:"subagent"` client:
  - llama.cpp marker with `/props` returning 404: base sent no header; head sent `X-Task-Class: subagent`.
  - Ollama with no `/api/version`, or with `/api/show` returning 404: header sent.
  - vLLM (`owned_by` vllm) with `/version` returning 404: header sent.
  - `NEXUS_SERVER_PROBE=0` with a llama.cpp marker: header sent.
  - After a successful identification, a rediscovery where `/models` returns 500 resets the kind to `unknown` (`serverKindCache.delete(ep)` at `client.ts:1139`), and the header is sent. This happens on the periodic refresh (`refreshCapabilities`, `CAPABILITY_TTL_MS`), whose comment says an unreadable catalog "keeps the last valid advertisement". The client and the agent now disagree on that.
  - In the same rediscovery case, vLLM also loses `strict` and the root `/tokenize` fallback.
- `test/task_class.test.ts` is unchanged and covers only the success path (llama.cpp marker with `/props` OK, then gateway).
- The fix is to decide the header from the catalog-level kind (`serverKindOf(entry)`), separately from handshake-verified adaptation. Also keep the previous kind when rediscovery returns `unavailable`.

**MEDIUM: the matrix runner does not enforce "only the verified installed candidate".**
- It checks a `.provenance.json` inside the caller-supplied `installRoot` (`eval/tool_grammar_matrix.mjs:259-270`). That file is self-attested JSON. Nothing ties it to the files under `lib/cli/dist`, the archive contents, or `MANIFEST.sha256`. `install.sh` checks the manifest at install time, but the runner never does.
- I demonstrated three bypasses against a copy of the runner:
  - A forged `.provenance.json`, a hand-written `lib/cli/dist` and an unrelated "archive" file were accepted: `passed: true`, with the archive's SHA recorded.
  - A symlinked `lib` pointing outside `installRoot` ran the outside runtime. `path.resolve` is used and there is no `realpath`.
  - Swapping the `lib` symlink right after the provenance read ran the swapped runtime (verify-then-import TOCTOU).
- The hand-written fixture in the committed test is itself this pattern.
- A caller-supplied `runtime` or `tools` option is rejected (own property), and an inherited `runtime` is never read. Env vars cannot substitute the runtime. `NEXUS_SERVER_PROBE=0` fails closed with a "provider identity mismatch" error. A wrong pinned `archiveSha256` is rejected.
- The regression test is genuinely RED without the guard. With the `Object.hasOwn(options,"runtime")` line removed, the test fails with `Missing expected rejection` (9 pass, 1 fail). But the guard is cosmetic, because the option is never consumed.
- The fix is to realpath `installRoot`, verify `MANIFEST.sha256` plus the archive-to-install link, and verify once and import from the same resolved path.
- The evidence fields `serverVersion`, `imageDigest` and `modelDigest` are config-attested. They are not compared with what the server reports. I did not check whether the plan intends that.

**MEDIUM-LOW: the vLLM identity check is weak.**
- `vllmCatalogMarker` is true for any `max_model_len` or `context_length` entry, because `parseAdvertisement` sets `via:"vllm"` for those (`provider_capabilities.ts:122`).
- I tested a catalog with only `max_model_len` and no `owned_by`, plus a `/version` response: kind became `vllm` and `strict:true` was sent.
- Any non-vLLM server with a `/version` route would be misidentified. I believe SGLang exposes one, but I did not verify that.
- The commit's own test (`client_tool_grammar.test.ts:51`) uses this shape, so it is by design, but it is weaker than the "generic catalog stays unknown" wording in the plan. Requiring `owned_by` vllm would be stricter.

**LOW and nits:**
- The WP-1107-PLAN AC4 test names do not exist in the repo. Missing are "client omits constrained fields for unknown and unsupported providers", "generic context catalog remains unknown…", and the four "provider identity accepts…" names. Substance is partly covered by other tests.
- `identityCached` at `client.ts:1156` is effectively dead, because the cache is deleted at line 1139.
- `docs/LOCAL_SERVERS.md` is unchanged. It still says vLLM is read directly from `max_model_len` and lists only the old probes under `NEXUS_SERVER_PROBE`.
- `adaptToolDefinitionsForServer` throws a TypeError if an allowlisted tool name ever has an optional array or object parameter. That would break every vLLM request instead of falling back. It is unreachable with the current registry.
- An Ollama `/api/show` response whose `model` field differs from the configured name (for example `:latest`) demotes the endpoint to unknown. I did not verify whether real Ollama sends that field.
- The new probes send the same origin-scoped credential as the existing `/props` probe, with `redirect:"error"`. I found no new leakage.
- Tool names and schemas are never placed into grammar text in this commit. The adapter works on JSON, restricted to the allowlisted names.
- It runs after the egress sanitization step, and unknown, llama.cpp, Ollama, gateway and LM Studio kinds return the same array reference unchanged.

## Q1: changed fixtures and assertions
I ran the 3eea888a test files against the 5fde750a source. Only three old assertions fail, and all three are legitimate updates to the new identity rule. None hides a regression by itself:
- **Ollama (`server_context_discovery`):** the old test fails with `via 'catalog'` instead of `'ollama'`, because there is no `/api/version` and the kind is now unknown. The update adds `GET /api/version` and expects it in the request sequence.
- **vLLM (`server_context_discovery`):** the old test fails only on the request sequence (an extra `GET /version`). Context discovery still returns 16384 (probe case 7, which has `owned_by` vllm but no `/version`).
- **`tokens`:** the old test fails with `HTTP 404`, because an unidentified vLLM no longer gets the root `/tokenize` URL. This is a real consequence of the rule, but real vLLM answers `/version`.
- **`standalone_profiles`:** the old test passes against the new source, and the change only adds a detected-kind assertion, so it is strengthened.
- **`model_proxy`:** only adds `/version` and `/api/version` routes for profile emulation.
- **`provider_capabilities` and the matrix wrapper:** additions only.
- **The 33 failures in `/tmp/wp1107-full-gate-final4.log`:** the ones I checked were host or environment issues (unbuilt `nexus-tui`, mount allowlist paths). Three were the identity-rule tests above, plus the Ollama standalone profile and a standalone server-profile run test (`eval_dataset`; I did not read its failure detail).
- **Coverage lost:** nothing asserts "context still discovered for a vLLM catalog without `/version`", and the vLLM discovery test does not assert the detected kind.
- **Coupling:** Ollama context discovery is now coupled to the `/api/version` handshake, so an Ollama proxy that exposes `/api/show` but not `/api/version` loses its context. This is a deliberate-looking tightening, but it goes beyond what the plan requires.

|---|---|---|---|

`npx tsc --noEmit` exited 0 with no output.

## Not verified
- Live provider behaviour: no real vLLM, llama.cpp or Ollama server. I did not test whether a vLLM build accepts or enforces `strict`, and the commit has no retry if the server rejects it with a 400. I also did not test SGLang's `/version`.
- The full `npm test` and `make test` runs, and the author's 2342/2347 claim. I only parsed the final7 log counts and confirmed its SHA prefix.
- The `/model` picker TUI end-to-end test (it needs `nexus-tui`, which I did not build). I covered provider switching only by reading `setModel`, the static `serverKindCache`, and the `providerId` guards.
- The null failures come from the core built from this commit and called through `RustCoreBridge.executeTool`, not from a full agent loop.
- The packaged installer layout. I checked only that real installed trees (v1.1.1) have `lib/cli/dist/{client,parser,core/capabilities}.js`, a `.provenance.json` with a 40-character `revision`, and `MANIFEST.sha256`.
- Whether `NEXUS_SERVER_PROBE` from `config.env` reaches `process.env`.

  - `write_file {overwrite:null}` returns `Invalid write_file arguments: invalid type: null, expected a boolean`.

content.text:
The WP-1107 reviewer came back **REQUEST CHANGES** on `5fde750a`, so that commit can't ship as it is. I posted the full review on PR #402, logged it in the claims log, and asked codex-root to fix it. I verified the key finding by reading the committed code.

**HIGH: vLLM strict mode makes `write_file` and `run_command` fail.**
- **Cause:** the provider adapter turns every optional parameter into a required nullable one, so a strict-mode model sends values like `overwrite: null` and `background: null`. The Rust core declares those as plain booleans and rejects the nulls: `Invalid write_file arguments: invalid type: null, expected a boolean`.
- **Evidence:** the reviewer built the core and reproduced it. I confirmed the plain-`bool` fields in `file_ops.rs:37` and `runner.rs:19`.
- **Why the tests passed:** the matrix scores a call as valid if it fits the adapted schema, which allows null. A vLLM run could score 100% while every `write_file` and `run_command` call fails when executed.

**Other findings:**
- **MEDIUM, privacy rule:** REQ-PRV-109 (no `X-Task-Class` header to standalone local servers unless configured) only holds when the server handshake succeeds. A failed handshake now sends the header, and so does a periodic rediscovery that fails. The reviewer reproduced this at head but not at the base. `task_class.test.ts` covers only the success path.
- **MEDIUM, evidence boundary:** the matrix runner still doesn't enforce "only the verified installed candidate". It trusts a self-written `.provenance.json`. The reviewer got a forged install accepted, a symlink to outside code run, and a swap between check and use run. The new regression test is real, but it guards a check that does nothing.
- **MEDIUM-LOW:** vLLM identity is weak. Any catalog with `max_model_len` plus a `/version` route is classed as vLLM and gets `strict` on.
- **Test changes:** the changed fixtures are legitimate updates to the new identity rule, with no weakening found.

The earlier "all green" gate missed all of this, because the tests didn't cover it. The WP-1105 reviewer is still running.

The decision is yours. Fixing it means codex-root fixes these (regression tests first), reruns the gate, and I re-review. That adds another cycle, probably a few hours. The alternative is to ship 1.1.2 on the earlier qualified `3eea888a` without these provider changes. That puts the earlier deferral back, and gate G1.1-4 would not be claimable. I'm continuing with the fix route unless you say otherwise. Nothing is tagged or published.

<result># Independent review: WP-1105 deterministic code evaluators as of 5fde750a

**Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES.** The sandbox containment is solid, and the telemetry counts each call once, including subagents. But `typecheck_clean` can pass without measuring anything, and the `syntax_ast` default can fail honest runs. I'd fix F1–F3 before relying on these evaluators for scores.

Setup: detached worktree `~/nexus-wt/rv-wp1105` at 5fde750a, isolated HOME/XDG, `cli/node_modules` copied from main. Main's lockfile differs slightly from this commit's. The worktree is removed. No push, post or edit in any checkout. Mutations ran in non-git copies under the scratchpad.

## Test counts
- **`code_evaluators.test.ts`:** 22 tests, 22 pass, 0 fail.
- **`parser_safety.test.ts`:** 12 pass. **`parser_single_quote.test.ts`:** 10 pass.
- **`eval/dataset.test.mjs`:** 12 pass. **`eval/package_runtime.test.mjs`:** 2 pass, 3 skipped, 0 fail.
- **`npx tsc --noEmit`:** exit 0.
- **`eval_dataset.test.ts`:** 1 test, failed. Its output says "compiler exposure could not be checked; refusing qualification". The run was refused before any evaluator ran, so I read it as a host-environment limit, not an evaluator defect.

## Findings, ranked by severity

**F1 (MEDIUM): `typecheck_clean` passes vacuously when the checker cannot run on either side.**
- Evidence: `typecheck_clean.mjs:41-49` tolerates any failing baseline as long as the candidate adds no new diagnostic lines.
- I ran the real sandbox with `node ./node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc` and no node_modules in either workspace. The result was `passed:true, score:1`, with 12 identical "Cannot find module" lines on both sides (`vacuous.mjs`).
- It also passed when the candidate had a syntax error the checker never saw.
- A bwrap setup failure that exits 1 with the same stderr on both sides passes the same way.
- Suggested fix: require the baseline to be a recognised state, for example exit 0 or a task-supplied diagnostic regex such as `error TS\d+`.

**F2 (MEDIUM): `build` and `typecheck_clean` run candidate-modified build config, so a candidate can game them.**
- Evidence: `run.mjs:308` passes `candidateWorkspace: ws`, the agent-modified tree. Hardened mode's `configChanges` refusal applies only to the hidden and regression checks.
- With real tsc, a candidate that rewrote `tsconfig.json` to `"files":["empty.ts"]` while keeping a new error file got `passed:true`, 0 candidate diagnostics (`gaming.mjs`).
- A candidate that honestly added a second error was correctly failed.
- Mitigations: pin the config from the baseline, or require `diff_boundary` to cover config files. The README doesn't say this.

**F3 (MEDIUM): `syntax_ast` fed with the runner's default file list false-fails honest agents.**
- Evidence: `runner.mjs:162` sets `files = spec.files ?? changedFiles`, which includes deleted and non-source paths.
- A scenario with an edited `src/a.ts`, a deleted `src/old.ts` and an edited `README.md` gave `passed:false`. The failures were `README.md: unsupported source extension` and `src/old.ts: ENOENT`.
- Any task that doesn't set `spec.files` can never pass if the agent deletes a file or edits a non-code file.

**F4 (LOW-MEDIUM): evaluator commands have no memory, pid or disk limits.**
- Evidence: `command.mjs` calls `runProcess(spec, {outputLimit})` with no `resources`, so `spawnContained` takes its uncontained branch (`resources.mjs:115`).
- Inside the sandbox:
  - `/proc/self/cgroup` is the user's session scope.
  - `/tmp` is a 24 GB tmpfs (about half of RAM).
  - `/workspace` is the real disk.
  - 300 background sleepers started with no cap (304 pids visible).
- Only wall time (default 120 s) and a 4 MiB output cap bound a candidate fork bomb or memory hog. Agent runs under run.mjs get a cgroup contract; the evaluators don't.

- **Test gaps:** some mutations survived, including the sibling-directory escape and the per-turn telemetry reset.

Codex's claim holds so far. The run is still in progress, though, and it is testing uncommitted code, not a commit.

**What's running**
- **The run:** a full `make test` that codex-root calls "CI-layout". It runs from a new Git-backed worktree, `v112-wp1107-final-git-20261104`. It has been going about 32 minutes and holds SUITE.
- **What is under test:** `7f915894` plus 12 modified files and 1 new test file. These are uncommitted fixes in that worktree. They match the findings from my reviews:
  - `agent.ts`, `client.ts` and `provider_capabilities.ts`
  - the matrix runner `eval/tool_grammar_matrix.mjs`
  - new tests, including `vllm_nullable_dispatch.test.ts` and 124 added lines in `task_class.test.ts`
- **So codex-root did pick up the review.** There is still no commit, no push, and no claims-log note saying so.

**The durable-history claim**
- **Earlier run:** the 07:35 run (`wp1107-final-git-make-test.log`) failed at least 62 top-level cases. A tool session expired at `step_loop.test.ts`. Its log names several durable-history failures.
- **Current run so far:** 731 passed and 0 failed so far (excluding the expected noise from inference-error output). The six earlier durable-history cases I checked, which cover restart during waiting, a durable operation over the workload, death after archive, and two compaction recovery cases, now pass. Two earlier failures, "AC3a: run --resume --step resumes durable state" and "AC3b: /step resumes saved objective after REPL restart", haven't been reached yet.
- **What the earlier failures were:** codex-root's own notes say they came from an invalid setup, not source defects. An archive snapshot had no `.git`, and the core directory was in the wrong place. I can only confirm the setup fix is consistent with the passing results. I haven't proven it was the cause.

**Caveats**
- **Nothing binds the result to a commit yet.** The fixes need committing, and the gate then has to run on that exact commit. Otherwise it says nothing about a head.
- **Clock skew in the log.** codex-root's heartbeats are labelled UTC but run about 2 hours 45 minutes ahead of real UTC (real time is 08:18, its heartbeat says 11:02). I'll go by file times and running processes for the silence rule, not its timestamps.
- **Not re-reviewed.** I haven't looked at the uncommitted fixes, only their file names. The independent re-review waits for the commit.

When it is committed, I'll re-review the delta from the REQUEST CHANGES findings.

<result>**Verdict on b032791e: REQUEST CHANGES.** Findings 1, 3 and 4 are fixed. Finding 2 is only partly fixed: the header leak is closed, but the server kind is still dropped on an unreadable rediscovery.

I built the Rust core in the worktree, drove `AutonomousAgent.dispatchToolCall` against the real `harness-core`, and removed the worktree at the end. My scratch scripts are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-mike-nexus-code/ee800dc3-6bb6-4e55-89e6-d6c2e85af4b6/scratchpad/`.

## Status of the four findings

**1. HIGH, null optional args: FIXED**
- Every optional field of the four allowlisted tools reaches the real core without error, whether passed alone as null or all together. Fields:
  - read_file: start_line, end_line, offset, length
  - write_file: overwrite
  - edit_file: replace_all
  - run_command: cwd, timeout_secs, shell, background, service_name
- The agent only strips `write_file.overwrite` and `run_command.background`, `timeout_secs` and `shell`. The other nulls are forwarded and the Rust side accepts them because those fields are `Option<_>`. This relies on core types and a hardcoded TS list staying in sync.
- Required fields given as null are still rejected before dispatch (FAIL-002) for path, content, old_content, new_content and command. Nothing is defaulted and nothing is written.
- Null and explicit values are told apart correctly:
  - `overwrite:null` on an existing file is refused (default false), the same as `false`, and `true` overwrites.
  - `replace_all:null` on an ambiguous edit is refused, and `true` replaces both occurrences.
  - `content:""`, `shell:""`, `cwd:""` and `timeout_secs:0` are kept and not stripped.
- All model-originated dispatch goes through `dispatchToolCall` (3 call sites).
- Mutation: with the strip block removed, `vllm_nullable_dispatch.test.ts` fails with "invalid type: null, expected a boolean".

**2. MEDIUM, REQ-PRV-109 X-Task-Class: PARTIAL**

I ran the same scenarios against 7f915894 (extracted to scratch) and b032791e. "Known" below means the kind had been detected before the rediscovery.

| Scenario | 7f915894 header | b032791e header |
|---|---|---|
| llama.cpp `/props` 404 | sent | suppressed |
| Ollama no `/api/version` | sent | suppressed |
| Ollama `/api/show` 404 | sent | suppressed |
| vLLM `/version` 404 | sent | suppressed |
| `NEXUS_SERVER_PROBE=0` (llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM) | sent | suppressed |
| bare catalog, or no `/models` at all | sent | suppressed |
| gateway, normal discovery | sent | sent |
| rediscovery `/models` 503, bad JSON or dropped connection, known llama.cpp/Ollama/vLLM | sent | suppressed |
| same, known gateway | sent | sent (kind retained) |

- **Not fixed:** a known llama.cpp, Ollama or vLLM endpoint falls to kind `unknown` on those unreadable-catalog rediscoveries, and also on `/models` 404 and "model not listed". For vLLM that means `strict` is lost and the `/tokenize` root fallback is lost. Identical at 7f915894 and b032791e.
- The agent keeps the last advertisement (`via: vllm`) and still tries token counting, so the two disagree.

content.text:
The delta review of `b032791e` came back REQUEST CHANGES, but most of the earlier problems are fixed. I posted it on #402 and logged it. Nothing is tagged or pushed.

**Status of the four WP-1107 findings:**
- **HIGH, null arguments: fixed.** The reviewer drove every optional field of `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file` and `run_command` through the real Rust core, alone and all-null, and none fail now. A null on a required field is still rejected. `false`, `0` and empty strings are not stripped. The test fails if the fix is removed.
- **MEDIUM, matrix runner: fixed.** It rejected forged provenance, a forged manifest, symlinks, and a swap between check and use. It runs only a private verified copy.
- **MEDIUM-LOW, vLLM identity: fixed.** `max_model_len` plus a `/version` route is no longer enough, but a real vLLM response is still recognised.
- **MEDIUM, task-class header: partly fixed.** The privacy leak is closed for failed handshakes and unreadable rediscovery, and the tests are real. What remains is that a known llama.cpp, Ollama or vLLM endpoint still drops to "unknown" when its model list can't be read on rediscovery. vLLM then loses strict mode and the `/tokenize` fallback while the agent keeps its old information. The fix is to keep the previous kind when rediscovery is unavailable. This is not a leak, so the severity is lower than the original.

**New, lower findings:**
- **Null stripping:** it applies only to the copy that gets dispatched. Read tracking still sees the raw nulls under vLLM strict, so it is silently degraded. Fixing it at the parse step would also remove the hardcoded per-tool list.
- **Smaller items:** a transient `/version` failure downgrades vLLM, matrix `sourceCommit` is only compared with the self-written record, and pinning the archive digest is optional.
- **Tests:** the sweep of eleven focused test files and `tsc` is green (about 120 tests). No assertion was weakened.

The WP-1105 evaluator findings (F1–F3) are still open, because this commit touches none of those files.

To clear the review, codex-root needs to fix the rediscovery kind retention and the evaluator findings, or say they are deferred. If we defer them, the release notes must say so plainly. Its exact-head gate on `b032791e` is still running, with a heartbeat at 09:00 UTC, and it still holds the version and qualification claims. You may want to tell it to take the three evaluator findings too. I'll check again at 09:14 UTC.

- **The commit:** `0d506762` ("close WP-1105 and WP-1107 review findings"), made at 10:56 UTC on top of `b032791e`. It changes 15 files (+744/−108) and is still local only. It claims to cover both sets of findings:
  - **WP-1107:** keeping a known server kind when rediscovery is unreadable, null normalisation in the client, and a source-commit check in the matrix runner.
  - **WP-1105:** pinning the evaluator configuration, with changes to `runner.mjs`, `syntax_ast.mjs`, `typecheck_clean.mjs` and `eval/run.mjs`.
- **Gate:** codex-root holds SUITE for an exact committed-head `make test` plus security gates on `0d506762`. It started at 10:58 UTC and its heartbeat was current at 11:09.
- **Reviewer 1, WP-1107 half:** they check whether the rediscovery kind retention is real and doesn't go stale or leak a wrong header or strict flag to a different server. They also check the null normalisation under vLLM strict for every optional field, the transient `/version` failure, and the matrix-runner bypasses. Each new test gets a mutation check, and the focused sweep and `tsc` run.
- **Reviewer 2, WP-1105 half:** they re-run my three scenarios: `typecheck_clean` passing when the checker can't run, a rewritten `tsconfig` hiding an error, and `syntax_ast` failing honest runs that delete or edit non-source files. They try other config routes (`package.json` scripts, `extends` chains, `node_modules`, build files), watch for anything that now fails open or fails honest runs, and report whether the lower items (limits, timeouts, command paths, line-shift false failures) were fixed, deferred or untouched.

Both have the same constraints as before: their own worktrees, focused test files only, and no SUITE claim. codex-root still holds the version and qualification claims. I'll check again at 11:40 UTC and post each verdict on #402 as it arrives.

**F1 (typecheck passed vacuously): FIXED at 0d506762, but 05913af5 probably reopens it.**
- Run with the real sandbox and real `tsc`:
  - No `node_modules` on either side now gives `infrastructureFailure` and `passed:false`.
  - A candidate syntax error with no `node_modules` also fails.
  - With `node_modules` present, the candidate's syntax error appears as a new TS1109 diagnostic.
- Unit cases: identical "Cannot find module" lines on both sides fail, and so do identical `bwrap:` setup failures.
- The gate is a hard-coded `error TS\d+:` regex, not the "task-supplied diagnostic regex" you described. Checkers that do not print TS codes (eslint, mypy, `cargo check`) always fail when the baseline already has errors. That fails closed but is undocumented. `eval/evaluators/code/README.md` and `SPEC-EVALUATION` still say `cargo check` is supported and still describe the old rule.
- Residual gap: identical recognised config errors on both sides, such as TS5057 (no tsconfig found), still pass vacuously. Low severity.
- 05913af5 changes the regex to `\berror(?:\s+TS\d+|\[E\d+\])?:` with the `/i` flag. The code group is now optional, so any line containing `error:` counts as recognised. That includes Node's `Error: Cannot find module '...'` and probably many sandbox errors.
- If so, F1 scenario 1 (no `node_modules`, identical lines on both sides) goes back to `passed:true`. This is from reading the diff, **not verified (host reserved)**. The fix is to require a Rust code (`error\[E\d+\]:`) or a TS code, not an optional one. The new test should include "Error: Cannot find module" on both sides.

**F2 (candidate-modified build config): PARTIAL.**
- Now blocked (real tsc):
  - `tsconfig.json` rewritten to `"files":["empty.ts"]`.
  - A new error file with `"include":["nothing"]`.
  - `tsconfig.build.json`.
  - An `extends` chain through `config/base.json`.
  - `package.json` scripts: a candidate with `"build":"true"` still fails because the baseline package.json is used.
  - A `scripts/build.js` rewrite.
  - `.tsbuildinfo` incremental state (the new diagnostic was still seen).
  - A patched `node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc` (no extension, so not overlaid).
- Still open:
  - **node_modules shadowing.** Rewriting `node_modules/typescript/lib/tsc.js` to `process.exit(0)` while keeping a type error gave `build` and `typecheck_clean` both `passed:true`. The overlay copies every candidate-changed `.ts/.js/.rs/.py`, `node_modules` included.
  - **Any other in-repo build helper** is overlaid as "source". `tools/check.js` rewritten to `exit(0)` made `build` pass. The same applies to `build.rs`, `setup.py`, `conftest.py` and the like. Only `*.config.*` and `scripts/{build,compile,typecheck}.*` are excluded.
- The honest candidate who legitimately edits `tsconfig.json` or `package.json` is not wrongly failed on source checks. A new `.d.ts` and a tsconfig edit that includes a new `lib/` dir both passed. The edited config is ignored silently, though, and that is not documented. Candidate config changes are neither reported nor failed.

**F3 (syntax_ast default list): FIXED, with one pre-existing exception.**
- Edit `src/a.ts`, delete `src/old.ts`, edit `README.md`: passes, and `files` is only `src/a.ts`.
- Still failing as required:
  - A broken `.ts` edit.
  - A broken `.TS`.
  - A broken `.ts` while another file is renamed to `.txt`.
  - A symlink to `/etc/passwd`.
  - A dangling `.ts` symlink.
- Passing as intended: only-README edited, only-deletion, a directory named `foo.ts`.
- An explicit `files` list that includes a deleted path still fails with ENOENT, which is the old behaviour.
- A broken file renamed to `.txt` is skipped. That is inherent to the design.
- Pre-existing, not in this commit: `node --check` returns 0 on ESM-syntax `.js` such as `export const a = ;` under Node v24.11.1, so syntax errors in ambiguous `.js` files pass. This is a false pass in `parsers.mjs`.

**Lower items.**
- **F4 (memory/pid/disk limits): untouched.** `command.mjs`, `isolate.mjs` and `parsers.mjs` have no diff.
- **F5 (parser timeout, 65 MB .ts blocking 62.9 s): untouched.** The TS parser is still in-process with no timeout, and the Node and Python child checks keep their 30 s timeout.

## 18-row typecheck rule table
- I compared the old and new `typecheck_clean` with a fake runner. All the rules you listed hold.
  - Silent non-zero fails.
  - Fewer diagnostics with a different non-zero exit passes.
  - Baseline 0 plus candidate non-zero fails.
  - Duplicates are counted.
  - A crash or timeout fails.
- Only three rows differ from before. Identical non-TS failures on both sides, identical bwrap failures, and non-TS baseline errors (eslint-style) went from pass to fail.
- `statusRegression` is now effectively dead.
- The 0d506762 table was not re-run against 05913af5.

## New findings, ranked

1. **HIGH, fail-open.** `build` and `typecheck_clean` now run in baseline plus an overlay of only `.ts/.mts/.cts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx/.rs/.py` candidate files.
   - Edits to any other file are invisible to the build: `.go`, `.c`, `.java`, `.json`, `.css`, `.vue`, `.sh`.

2. **MEDIUM.** The `node_modules` and build-helper overlay vectors listed under F2.
3. **MEDIUM, 05913af5.** The optional-code regex described under F1 likely reopens the vacuous pass.
4. **MEDIUM, honest-run failure.**
   - The runner now takes two full workspace snapshots, baseline and candidate, even for build-only tasks.
   - A ~54k-file `node_modules` gave `workspace snapshot refused: traversal deadline exceeded` after 5 s, so `build` failed.

// Runs the CLI test suite with a throwaway HOME so no test (or anything it spawns: the sidecar, the TUI, PTY drivers)
// can read or write the operator's ~/.nexus or ~/.config/nexus. The real home is passed as NEXUS_TEST_REAL_HOME so the
// guard test can prove the isolation held. Arguments are test files; none means every test/*.test.ts.
// NEXUS_KEEP_TEST_HOME=1 keeps the temporary home for inspection.
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import fs from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const cli = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..");
const realHome = os.homedir();
const home = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "nexus-test-home-"));

const files = process.argv.length > 2
  ? process.argv.slice(2)
  : [
      ...fs.readdirSync(path.join(cli, "test")).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".test.ts")).sort().map((f) => path.join("test", f)),
      path.resolve(cli, "../eval/dataset.test.mjs"),
      path.resolve(cli, "../eval/package_runtime.test.mjs"),
    ];

const env = {
  ...process.env,
  HOME: home,
  XDG_CONFIG_HOME: path.join(home, ".config"),
  XDG_DATA_HOME: path.join(home, ".local", "share"),
  XDG_STATE_HOME: path.join(home, ".local", "state"),
  XDG_CACHE_HOME: path.join(home, ".cache"),
  NEXUS_TEST_REAL_HOME: realHome,
};
// Rust and Node toolchains installed per user keep working under the throwaway home.
for (const [key, dir] of [["CARGO_HOME", ".cargo"], ["RUSTUP_HOME", ".rustup"]]) {
  if (!env[key] && fs.existsSync(path.join(realHome, dir))) env[key] = path.join(realHome, dir);
}

const tsx = path.join(cli, "node_modules", ".bin", "tsx");
const result = spawnSync(tsx, ["--test", "--test-concurrency=1", ...files], { cwd: cli, env, stdio: "inherit" });

if (process.env.NEXUS_KEEP_TEST_HOME === "1") console.error(`test home kept at ${home}`);

# Nexus Code v1.1.2

**Nexus Code v1.1.2** targets the full WP-1101–WP-1108 roadmap that was originally planned for v1.1.0. The v1.1.0 release failed and published no release files; v1.1.1 is the published predecessor. Version numbers are immutable, so the roadmap work is assigned to v1.1.2.

## Release scope and status

The intended scope is the complete [WP-1101–WP-1108 roadmap](../v1.1.0/ROADMAP.md), together with any already-approved corrective changes needed for the candidate. The operation message-delivery correction described below remains relevant context for the v1.1.1 predecessor.

This document records the target scope; it does not claim that the roadmap is implemented or qualified. As of this note, roadmap implementation and v1.1.2 qualification remain incomplete; completion requires recording the applicable evidence. Work-package completion, exact-head test and type gates, independent review, release-candidate qualification, and publication are still required before v1.1.2 can be called released. Track implementation and evidence in the work-package plans and release qualification record.

## Fixed

### A crash-resumed unit no longer receives a multi-message prompt's later messages twice

When a work unit's prompt carried two or more operator or inter-unit messages, and Nexus stopped after submitting that prompt but before the unit's result was saved, resume recognised only the **first** message as already submitted. Every later message from that prompt was injected into the unit's conversation again.

Resume now recognises each message in a submitted prompt's messages block, whatever its position. Matching is still limited to prompts that Nexus issued (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`, from v1.1.1), so marker text in model output, tool output, or files cannot suppress a message.

- Impact in v1.1.1: the duplicated message was advisory context only. No message was lost, and no `TurnResult`, verification, or acceptance outcome was affected.
- Regression coverage: the post-prompt crash test in `cli/test/operation_release_review.test.ts` now carries two messages. It asserts that each message appears once in the durable history and is acknowledged once.

## Correction to the v1.1.1 notes

The v1.1.1 notes say that a recipient receives undelivered messages "at most once". That holds for prompts carrying a single message. For prompts carrying several messages, v1.1.1 could re-inject the second and later messages after a post-submission crash, as described above. v1.1.2 makes the statement hold in both cases. `docs/releases/v1.1.1.md` carries a matching addendum.

## Runtime requirements

Unchanged from v1.1.1: Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (local or an explicitly selected provider). The archive does not include Node.js. Rust and Cargo are not required at runtime.

## Upgrade

Operation records are unchanged: operation schema version 2, as in v1.1.1. No migration runs, and v1.1.1 can read records written by v1.1.2.

## Qualification

The multi-message resume correction is present in the candidate branch (`c0afc44c`). It is one corrective change within the larger roadmap scope, not the definition of this release. Qualification must cover the complete WP-1101–WP-1108 scope on the exact final candidate, including its full test and type gates, package and upgrade checks, independent review, and installed-candidate acceptance. v1.1.1 qualification or evidence from an earlier candidate does not qualify the final v1.1.2 candidate.

# Nexus Code v1.1.2

**Maturity:** Stable release for Nexus Code v1.1.2, shipped **with known limitations** that the owner accepted explicitly. They are listed in full below, and the [qualification record](v1.1.2-qualification.md) carries the evidence and the open items.

v1.1.2 delivers the WP-1101 to WP-1108 roadmap that was originally planned for v1.1.0. The v1.1.0 release failed and published no release files, and v1.1.1 is the published predecessor. Version numbers are immutable, so the roadmap work is assigned to v1.1.2. No `v1.1.2-rc.*` tag was ever published; the candidates that carried those names are superseded.

## What is in this release

- **WP-1101, local OpenTelemetry tracing.** GenAI spans for turns, model requests, tool dispatch and compaction, written locally with payload-free attributes. Trace output is confined to the approved trace directory.

- **WP-1105, deterministic code evaluators.** AST, build, typecheck, diff-boundary and JSON-repair evaluators and tool-call syntax telemetry (`toolCallSyntax`). **The evaluators are a library: no dataset task uses them yet.** See the limitations below.
- **WP-1106, single-step loop mode.** `--step`, and `/step` in the REPL and the TUI, pause after one agent turn for operator confirmation.
- **WP-1107, bounded tool grammar and provider-specific strict tool schemas.** A bounded schema compiler, plus strict tool schemas for llama.cpp, vLLM and Ollama request paths. The 99.5% valid-tool-call target was **not measured** against live providers; see below.
- **WP-1108, dependency modernisation.** The pending Dependabot updates were triaged and merged. `cargo deny` is clean, there are no deprecated npm packages, and a CycloneDX SBOM is generated.

When a work unit's prompt carried two or more operator or inter-unit messages, and Nexus stopped after submitting that prompt but before the unit's result was saved, resume recognised only the **first** message as already submitted. Every later message from that prompt was injected into the unit's conversation again.

Resume now recognises each message in a submitted prompt's messages block, whatever its position. Matching is still limited to prompts that Nexus issued (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`, from v1.1.1), so marker text in model output, tool output, or files cannot suppress a message.

- Impact in v1.1.1: the duplicated message was advisory context only. No message was lost, and no `TurnResult`, verification, or acceptance outcome was affected.
- Regression coverage: the post-prompt crash test in `cli/test/operation_release_review.test.ts` carries two messages and asserts that each appears once in the durable history and is acknowledged once.

The v1.1.1 notes say that a recipient receives undelivered messages "at most once". That holds for prompts carrying a single message. ## Known limitations (owner waiver)

Independent reviewers examined the release source and returned REQUEST CHANGES on the WP-1105 evaluator work and on the WP-1107 provider work. The owner decided to ship v1.1.2 with the findings below open, and to fix only one of them (the `typecheck_clean` diagnostic pattern, commit `2dbe565b`). ### Not measured

- **Constrained decoding, gate G1.1-4: NOT MET, NOT MEASURED.** The target is at least 99.5% valid tool-call JSON across supported provider endpoints. The provider-specific strict schemas are connected and tested locally with mock servers. No measurement against live llama.cpp, vLLM or Ollama endpoints was made, because the shared gateway resource was held by another release stream. Do not read this release as having met that target.
- **Task quality.** The benchmark fixture checks execution and prompt boundaries, not task-solving or provider quality.

### Provider handling (WP-1107)

- **The server-kind cache never expires or invalidates.** A server kind learned for an endpoint is kept when a later model-list refresh is unreadable (503, bad JSON, dropped connection, 404 or the model not listed). If the server on that endpoint is replaced, the old kind and its strict flag can remain. A gateway kept this way sends the `X-Task-Class` header to a non-gateway server that replaced it on the same endpoint. The rule that standalone local servers do not receive `X-Task-Class` (REQ-PRV-109) therefore holds on the success path and for non-gateway kinds, not in that replacement case.

- **Request counting can turn off.** After a transient `/version` failure, or a 404 or missing-model refresh, a retained vLLM kind no longer matches the advertised source, so the agent probably reports that request counting is unavailable.
- **Matrix provenance is not bound to the checkout content.** The matrix runner now verifies the installed archive and the clean checkout commit, but any clean repository at the claimed commit passes.
- **Ollama identity.** A transient `/api/version` failure on a successful refresh still drops the kind to unknown.

### Code evaluators (WP-1105)

- **Fail-open overlay.** Build and typecheck run in the baseline workspace with only candidate edits to `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx`, `.rs` and `.py` files overlaid. Edits to any other file (`.go`, `.c`, `.json` and so on) are invisible to the build, so a change in one of those files that breaks the build can pass. Honest changes to such inputs, for example a new JSON module, can fail.
- **Shadowing.** A candidate can still shadow the checker through `node_modules` or an in-repo build helper, because those files are overlaid as source.
- **Large workspaces.** The runner takes two full workspace snapshots even for build-only tasks. A workspace with a very large `node_modules` is refused (5 second traversal deadline, 50,000 entries).

Unchanged from v1.1.1: Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (local or an explicitly selected provider). The archive does not include Node.js. Rust and Cargo are not required at runtime.

## Upgrade

Operation records are unchanged: operation schema version 2, as in v1.1.1. No migration runs, and v1.1.1 can read records written by v1.1.2.

## Qualification

The [qualification record](v1.1.2-qualification.md) states what was run, on which commit, with which result, and what was not run. In short: the exact source head passed the full local suite and security gates (counts in the record). Independent review of the WP-1105 and WP-1107 work was not an ACCEPT; its findings are the limitations above.

# Nexus Code v1.1.2

**Nexus Code v1.1.2** targets the full WP-1101–WP-1108 roadmap that was originally planned for v1.1.0. The v1.1.0 release failed and published no release files; v1.1.1 is the published predecessor. Version numbers are immutable, so the roadmap work is assigned to v1.1.2.

## Release scope and status

The intended scope is the complete [WP-1101–WP-1108 roadmap](../v1.1.0/ROADMAP.md), together with any already-approved corrective changes needed for the candidate. The operation message-delivery correction described below remains relevant context for the v1.1.1 predecessor.

This document records the target scope; it does not claim that the roadmap is implemented or qualified. As of this note, roadmap implementation and v1.1.2 qualification remain incomplete; completion requires recording the applicable evidence. Work-package completion, exact-head test and type gates, independent review, release-candidate qualification, and publication are still required before v1.1.2 can be called released. Track implementation and evidence in the work-package plans and release qualification record.

## Fixed

### A crash-resumed unit no longer receives a multi-message prompt's later messages twice

When a work unit's prompt carried two or more operator or inter-unit messages, and Nexus stopped after submitting that prompt but before the unit's result was saved, resume recognised only the **first** message as already submitted. Every later message from that prompt was injected into the unit's conversation again.

Resume now recognises each message in a submitted prompt's messages block, whatever its position. Matching is still limited to prompts that Nexus issued (`isSubmittedUnitPrompt`, from v1.1.1), so marker text in model output, tool output, or files cannot suppress a message.

- Impact in v1.1.1: the duplicated message was advisory context only. No message was lost, and no `TurnResult`, verification, or acceptance outcome was affected.
- Regression coverage: the post-prompt crash test in `cli/test/operation_release_review.test.ts` now carries two messages. It asserts that each message appears once in the durable history and is acknowledged once.

## Correction to the v1.1.1 notes

The v1.1.1 notes say that a recipient receives undelivered messages "at most once". That holds for prompts carrying a single message. For prompts carrying several messages, v1.1.1 could re-inject the second and later messages after a post-submission crash, as described above. v1.1.2 makes the statement hold in both cases. `docs/releases/v1.1.1.md` carries a matching addendum.

## Runtime requirements

Unchanged from v1.1.1: Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.35 or newer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (local or an explicitly selected provider). The archive does not include Node.js. Rust and Cargo are not required at runtime.

## Upgrade

Operation records are unchanged: operation schema version 2, as in v1.1.1. No migration runs, and v1.1.1 can read records written by v1.1.2.

## Qualification

The multi-message resume correction is present in the candidate branch (`c0afc44c`). It is one corrective change within the larger roadmap scope, not the definition of this release. Qualification must cover the complete WP-1101–WP-1108 scope on the exact final candidate, including its full test and type gates, package and upgrade checks, independent review, and installed-candidate acceptance. v1.1.1 qualification or evidence from an earlier candidate does not qualify the final v1.1.2 candidate.

  - v1.1.2.md intro: "v1.1.2 delivers the WP-1101 to WP-1108 roadmap…".
  - Qualification, WP-1107 row: "connect provider-specific strict tool schemas to llama.cpp, vLLM, and Ollama request paths".
  - Qualification, G1.1-4 row: "Provider-specific strict tool-schema requests are connected and tested locally against mock servers."
  - Qualification, WP-1107 row title: "GBNF tool grammar".

- Say "the CodeQL check passed (alert count not queried)".

The roadmap promised llama.cpp `grammar`, vLLM `guided_json`, Ollama `format` and the hybrid grammars; on top of that the 99.5% target was never measured, so G1.1-4 stays "not met, not measured". This is new information for you.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** still described v1.1.2 as a 2026-11-01 patch. It now says "Unreleased" with the real scope.
- **Limitations and the review table** were too weak or lossy in several places. I fixed them: build-configuration edits ignored, the HIGH rating on the fail-open overlay, the process-wide server-kind cache, a missing first WP-1105 review row, and a few word changes.
- **Verified correct:** every gate number and log hash, the version bump across all six files, no `v1.1.2*` tag on origin, #398/#396/#401 merged, and the links.
- **Not re-reviewed:** the corrected text was not re-reviewed, since the changes were mechanical. The report is on the PR.

**State:** PR #402 is ready for review at `fafbf6d5`. The security gates pass on it, and a check that nothing outside docs and `CHANGELOG.md` changed since `bd7fb1cf` came back empty. CI is rerunning on this head.

**For you:**
1. **Entire approval.** When CI is green, #402 will be waiting on your Entire approval. I won't approve it myself.
2. **ACCEPT rule.** The reviewer noted that your 2026-11-03 rule said "tag after independent ACCEPT", while your 2026-11-04 waiver covers the open findings. Please confirm that your Entire approval on the final head stands in for the ACCEPT.
3. **WP-1107 scope.** Please confirm you're happy shipping the reduced WP-1107.

Then I merge with a merge commit, close #400 after verifying its tree is contained, tag `v1.1.2`, and watch the release workflow. I'll check again at 18:52 UTC.

That is the point of WP-1106. The Entire 'Findings' gate fails on it. What do you want?

options.label: Fix the HIGH, rerun the gate (Recommended)
options.description: I make a minimal fix (apply the pause at the shared cycle boundary) in cli/src/agent.ts with a regression test written red first, claim the file, then rerun the full gate on the new head (about 1h45m), re-push docs, and wait for CI. About 2.5 to 3 hours before the merge is possible.

options.label: Ship with it, documented
options.description: Add it to the known limitations (--step can run past one turn when a turn has parallel read_file calls), and you dismiss or resolve the Entire finding with that note. Fastest, but --step does not do what its name says in that case.

options.label: Cut WP-1106 --step from the release
options.description: Remove nothing in code, but document --step as experimental/unreliable and exclude it from the release claims. Fastest honest option if you do not want a new gate.
